breakfast.name: Masala Dosa
ingredients: Rice batter (fermented overnight with urad dal)
Potato filling: potatoes, mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric, onion, green chili
instructions: The batter ferments overnight — rice and urad dal ground together, the fermentation creates the sour tang and crispiness
Heat a flat tawa or griddle until very hot
Pour a ladle of batter, spread in a thin circle from center outward
Drizzle ghee around the edges — the dosa should sizzle and turn golden
Spoon the spiced potato filling in a line down the center
Fold the dosa over the filling — crispy, golden, stuffed
Serve with coconut chutney and sambar
The crispiness of the dosa against the soft potato filling is the contrast
South Indian breakfast perfection — the fermentation technique is ancient food science
breakfast.description: South India's iconic fermented rice crêpe — batter fermented overnight for tang, spread paper-thin on a hot griddle until crispy, stuffed with spiced potato. The fermentation science and the dramatic griddle technique make masala dosa one of the most viral Indian foods globally.

breakfast.name: Chole Bhature
ingredients: Chole masala: coriander, cumin, garam masala, amchur, chili powder
Tea bag or pomegranate seeds (for dark color)
Bhature dough: flour, yogurt, oil, baking powder
instructions: Make chole: sauté onion until dark brown, add ginger-garlic paste
Add tomato, cook until oil separates — the patient onion-tomato base is key
Add all spices, fry until fragrant
Add chickpeas with liquid, simmer until thick and dark
Make bhature dough: flour, yogurt, oil, baking powder — rest 2 hours
Roll into circles, deep fry until puffed and golden — they balloon dramatically
The bhature puffing in oil is one of cooking's most satisfying visuals
Serve chole in a bowl with bhatura on the side, pickled onion, and green chutney
This is North India's (especially Delhi/Punjab) most beloved breakfast
breakfast.description: Delhi-Punjab's iconic breakfast — spicy dark chickpea curry with dramatically puffed fried bread. The bhatura ballooning in hot oil is one of the most satisfying cooking visuals on earth. Chole bhature is North India's most craved breakfast and a global viral food.

breakfast.name: Poha (Flattened Rice)
instructions: Rinse poha briefly — it softens in seconds, don't over-soak
Heat oil, add mustard seeds — let them pop and crackle
Add curry leaves, peanuts, fry until peanuts are golden
Add onion, green chili, turmeric, sauté
Add the softened poha, toss gently — it breaks if you're rough
Add salt, sugar (the tiny bit of sugar is key), lemon juice
Garnish with cilantro and serve with a wedge of lemon
This is Maharashtra's (Mumbai) everyday breakfast — fast, light, satisfying
breakfast.description: Maharashtra's everyday breakfast — flattened rice tossed with mustard seeds, peanuts, and turmeric in minutes. The mustard-seed crackle, the lemon squeeze, and the speed (10 minutes start to finish) make poha one of India's most practical and beloved morning dishes.

breakfast.name: Idli with Sambar
ingredients: Idli batter (fermented rice and urad dal — same family as dosa)
Sambar: toor dal, tamarind, sambar powder, vegetables (drumstick, carrot, onion)
Coconut chutney: fresh coconut, green chili, ginger
instructions: Pour fermented batter into idli molds — the fermentation makes them fluffy
Steam for 10-12 min until a toothpick comes out clean
They should be white, fluffy, and slightly sour from the fermentation
Make sambar: cook toor dal, add tamarind water, sambar powder, vegetables
Temper with mustard seeds, curry leaves, dried chilies in hot oil
Make coconut chutney: grind coconut with green chili, temper with mustard seeds
Serve idlis on a plate, sambar and chutney in bowls for dipping
Tear idli, dip in sambar — the soft idli soaks up the tangy lentil soup
South India's purest breakfast — steamed, fermented, probiotic, vegan
breakfast.description: South India's steamed rice cakes — soft, white, sour-fermented pillows served with tangy lentil-vegetable sambar and coconut chutney. Idli is arguably the healthiest breakfast on earth: steamed, fermented (probiotic), and naturally vegan. The simplicity is the genius.

breakfast.name: Paratha (Stuffed Flatbread)
ingredients: Filling options: spiced potato (aloo), cauliflower (gobi), paneer, radish (mooli)
instructions: Make whole wheat dough — soft and pliable, rest 15 min
Prepare filling: mashed potato with green chili, cumin, cilantro (for aloo paratha)
Take a dough ball, flatten, add filling in center, seal, roll out carefully
Cook on hot tawa with ghee — both sides golden and slightly charred
Press with a cloth while cooking — this ensures even cooking and puffing
The paratha should be flaky, golden, with visible layers
Serve with yogurt, pickle, and butter on top
Each region has signature fillings — Punjab does aloo, Rajasthan does pyaaz (onion)
This is North India's heartiest breakfast — carbs, fat, protein all in one
breakfast.description: North India's stuffed flatbread — whole wheat dough wrapped around spiced potato, cauliflower, or paneer, cooked with ghee on a griddle. Every North Indian home makes parathas differently, and the 'whose paratha is best' debate is eternal. The flaky layers and the ghee-sheen are the hooks.

lunch.name: Biryani (Hyderabadi Dum)
ingredients: Lamb or chicken (marinated in yogurt, spices)
Whole spices: cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaf
Dough (to seal the pot — dum technique)
instructions: Marinate meat in yogurt, ginger-garlic, chili, garam masala — 2+ hours
Fry sliced onions until deep golden-brown — birista, the soul of biryani
Parboil rice with whole spices — drain at 70% done
Layer in a heavy pot: meat on bottom, rice on top
Scatter fried onions, mint, cilantro, saffron milk between layers
Seal the pot with dough — this is the dum (steam-trapping) technique
Cook on very low heat for 45-60 min — the steam cooks everything together
Break the dough seal at the table — the fragrant steam that escapes is the moment
Each grain of rice should be separate, the meat tender, and the layers distinct
The bottom layer (the tah) should be slightly crispy from the ghee
lunch.description: Hyderabadi dum biryani — the most contested dish in India. Layers of marinated meat and saffron rice sealed with dough and slow-steamed. The dough-seal-breaking moment, the 'whose biryani is best' city wars, and the saffron-steamed fragrance make biryani India's most viral dish and one of the world's great rice preparations.

lunch.name: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
ingredients: Chicken (marinated in yogurt, ginger, garlic, chili, garam masala)
Tomato sauce: tomatoes, butter (lots), cream, cashews
Kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves — the secret ingredient)
instructions: Marinate chicken in yogurt and spices — minimum 2 hours, overnight is better
Grill or tandoor the chicken until charred — the char is essential
Make sauce: cook tomatoes until broken down, blend smooth with cashews
Add butter — generous, this is 'butter' chicken — cream, sugar, salt
Simmer sauce until rich, orange-red, and velvety
Add the charred chicken to the sauce
Finish with kasuri methi (crumble dried fenugreek over the top) and more cream
The kasuri methi is what makes butter chicken taste like butter chicken — don't skip
Serve with naan or rice — the sauce demands bread for scooping
Invented at Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi in the 1950s
lunch.description: Delhi's gift to the world — charcoal-grilled chicken in a rich, buttery, creamy tomato sauce finished with dried fenugreek. Invented at Moti Mahal in 1950s Delhi, butter chicken is now the world's most ordered Indian dish. The orange sauce, the cream swirl, and the naan-scooping technique are eternally viral.

lunch.name: Dal Makhani (Black Lentil Stew)
instructions: Soak black dal overnight — minimum 8 hours
Pressure cook or slow-cook dal until completely soft — this takes HOURS
The slow cooking is what makes restaurant-style dal makhani: 8-12 hours on low heat
Mash some dal against the pot — creates a creamy texture with some whole lentils
Make the tempering: butter, tomato, ginger, garlic, spices
Add the tempering to the dal, simmer together
Add cream and more butter — keep adding butter, this is makhani (buttery)
Finish with kasuri methi — the same fenugreek that defines butter chicken
The dal should be dark, creamy, thick, and impossibly rich
The slow-cooking-equals-flavor principle is fully proven by dal makhani
lunch.description: India's slow-cooked black lentil stew — urad dal simmered for 8+ hours with butter and cream until impossibly rich and creamy. Dal makhani proves that lentils + patience + butter = luxury. The 8-hour cooking time and the 'lentils can be THIS good?' revelation make it a viral vegetarian showcase.

lunch.name: Pav Bhaji (Mumbai Street Food)
ingredients: Bhaji: potatoes, cauliflower, peas, tomato, onion, capsicum
Pav bhaji masala (the special spice blend)
Lime, cilantro, raw onion for serving
instructions: Boil potatoes, cauliflower, peas until very soft — mash roughly
Sauté onion, tomato, capsicum in butter until soft
Add pav bhaji masala — fry until fragrant
Add mashed vegetables, mix well, add water for consistency
Mash everything together on the griddle with a flat spatula — the theatrical mashing
Add more butter — the butter should pool on top
Toast pav rolls on the same butter-covered griddle — both sides golden
Serve bhaji in a bowl, pav on the side, raw onion, lime, cilantro on top
The amount of butter used is genuinely alarming — and essential
This is Mumbai beach-street food — Juhu Beach at sunset with pav bhaji
lunch.description: Mumbai's most iconic street food — mixed vegetable mash cooked with an alarming amount of butter, served with buttered toasted bread rolls. The theatrical griddle-mashing and the butter-pooling-on-top visual are classic Mumbai street-food theater. Pav bhaji at Juhu Beach is a bucket-list food experience.

lunch.name: Fish Curry (Goan/Kerala)
ingredients: Fish (pomfret, kingfish, or any firm white fish)
instructions: Make masala paste: grind coconut, red chili, coriander, turmeric
Heat coconut oil, add mustard seeds — let crackle, add curry leaves
Sauté onion, ginger, garlic until golden
Add masala paste, fry until oil separates
Add coconut milk and water, bring to simmer
Add kokum or tamarind for sourness — the sour note is essential to coastal curry
Add fish pieces gently — do not stir, the fish breaks
Simmer 10-12 min until fish is just cooked through
The curry should be coconut-rich, sour, and bright orange-red
Serve with steamed rice — the curry-rice ratio matters
lunch.description: India's coastal fish curry — fresh fish simmered in coconut milk with kokum and spices. Goa and Kerala both claim the best version. The coconut-sour-spice balance and the 'don't stir or the fish breaks' technique are the hallmarks of India's coastal cooking tradition.

dinner.name: Tandoori Chicken
ingredients: Chicken (whole or pieces — leg quarters are best)
Yogurt marinade: yogurt, ginger, garlic, Kashmiri red chili, garam masala
Kashmiri red chili (for color — less heat, more color)
instructions: Make marinade: yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri chili, garam masala, lemon, mustard oil
Score the chicken deeply — the marinade must penetrate
Marinate overnight — minimum 4 hours but overnight is transformative
Cook in a tandoor (clay oven) at extreme heat — 300°C+
If no tandoor: oven at maximum heat on a wire rack, or charcoal grill
The extreme heat chars the outside while keeping the inside juicy
Baste with butter in the last few minutes
The chicken should be charred red-black outside, juicy and tender inside
Finish with a squeeze of lemon and chaat masala
Invented at Moti Mahal, Delhi — same restaurant that created butter chicken
dinner.description: India's most famous grilled chicken — yogurt-marinated, red from Kashmiri chili, charred in a tandoor clay oven at extreme heat. Invented at Moti Mahal in 1940s Delhi, tandoori chicken changed global food culture. The red char, the yogurt-tenderized juiciness, and the tandoor technique are perpetually viral.

dinner.name: Rogan Josh (Kashmiri Lamb)
ingredients: Kashmiri red chili (for the signature red color)
Onion (optional — some Kashmiri versions skip onion)
instructions: Bloom Kashmiri red chili in warm water — this creates the brilliant red color
Heat mustard oil until it smokes, then cool slightly
Brown lamb on all sides — build deep color
Add yogurt slowly, stirring constantly to prevent curdling
Add Kashmiri chili paste, fennel, ginger powder, whole spices
Simmer on very low heat for 90 min — Kashmiri cooking is patient
The oil should rise to the top and turn a brilliant red — rogan means oil, josh means heat
The sauce should be red, thick, and fragrant with fennel and cardamom
Finish with saffron — the Kashmir-Iran spice connection
This is Kashmir's royal dish — Mughal-era heritage
dinner.description: Kashmir's royal lamb stew — brilliant red from Kashmiri chili (color, not just heat), slow-cooked until the oil rises crimson. 'Rogan josh' means 'red oil heat.' The color, the Mughal-era heritage, and the patience required make rogan josh one of Indian cuisine's most prestigious and viral dishes.

dinner.name: Palak Paneer
instructions: Blanch spinach in boiling water 2 min, shock in ice water — keeps it bright green
Blend spinach smooth — the vibrant green purée is the base
Sauté cumin seeds in ghee until they crackle
Add onion, ginger-garlic, cook until golden
Add tomato, spices, cook until thick
Add the spinach purée, simmer 10 min
Add paneer cubes — the soft cheese in the green sauce is the visual
Finish with cream and butter
The green should be vibrant — overcooking turns it dull
Serve with naan — scoop the green sauce with bread
dinner.description: India's most famous vegetarian dish — cubes of soft paneer cheese in a vibrant green spinach sauce. Palak paneer proves that vegetarian food can be rich, satisfying, and beautiful. The bright green color and the 'cheese in spinach' concept have made it one of the most ordered Indian dishes worldwide.

dinner.name: Rajma Chawal (Kidney Bean Curry with Rice)
ingredients: Rajma (red kidney beans — soaked overnight, pressure cooked)
Rajma masala or garam masala, cumin, coriander
instructions: Soak rajma overnight — pressure cook until completely soft
Sauté onion until golden, add ginger-garlic paste
Add tomato, cook until oil separates
Add spices, fry until fragrant
Add cooked rajma with their liquid — the starchy liquid is the gravy base
Simmer 30 min until thick and creamy — the beans break down slightly, thickening the gravy
The gravy should coat the back of a spoon
Serve over steamed basmati rice with a squeeze of lime and cilantro
Rajma chawal is North India's Sunday lunch — every family makes it weekly
The comfort factor rivals any stew in the world
dinner.description: North India's Sunday lunch — red kidney beans simmered in spiced tomato gravy until thick and creamy, served over steamed rice. Rajma chawal is India's ultimate comfort food and the weekly ritual of millions of North Indian families. The simplicity and the 'beans over rice' concept resonate universally.

dinner.name: Thali (The Indian Meal Plate)
instructions: A thali is not a recipe — it's a concept: a complete, balanced meal on one plate
Cook a dal: toor dal with tempering (mustard seeds, curry leaves, chili)
Cook a dry sabzi: seasonal vegetables with spices
Cook a gravy dish: paneer or meat in a sauce
Make rice, make roti or naan
Arrange on a round plate or tray: rice in center, bowls of dal, sabzi, gravy around it
Add raita, pickle, papad, and a small sweet
Every region's thali is different: Gujarati is sweeter, Rajasthani is spicier, South Indian has sambar
The thali represents Indian food philosophy: balance of all six tastes in one meal
Unlimited thali restaurants let you eat as much as you want — they keep refilling
dinner.description: The Indian thali — a complete balanced meal on one plate: rice, dal, vegetables, bread, yogurt, pickle, and sweet. Every region's thali is different, and the concept of balancing all six tastes (sweet, sour, salty, bitter, pungent, astringent) in one meal is India's greatest food philosophy contribution.

snacks.name: Samosa
ingredients: Dough: flour, oil, carom seeds (ajwain), salt, water
Filling: potatoes (boiled, mashed), peas, cumin, coriander, garam masala, green chili, amchur
instructions: Make dough with oil and ajwain — rest 30 min
The dough should be flaky, not soft — the oil creates layers
Prepare filling: mash potatoes with peas and spices — let cool
Roll dough into ovals, cut in half — each half becomes a cone
Fill the cone with potato filling, seal edges with water
Deep fry in medium-hot oil — too hot and the outside burns before the dough cooks through
The oil temperature is the secret: start at 150°C, finish at 175°C
Fry until deep golden and crispy — 6-8 min
Serve with green chutney and tamarind chutney — the sweet-sour contrast
Samosas are India's universal snack — every state, every city, every corner
snacks.description: India's universal snack — crispy pastry triangles filled with spiced potato and peas, served with mint and tamarind chutneys. The double-fry temperature technique (low to cook through, high to crisp) and the worldwide spread of the samosa make it one of the most viral snacks on earth.

snacks.name: Pani Puri (Golgappa)
ingredients: Puris (crispy hollow balls — semolina and flour, fried)
Pani (flavored water): mint, cilantro, green chili, cumin, chaat masala, tamarind, lime
instructions: Make or buy crispy puris — they must be hollow inside
Make mint pani: blend mint, cilantro, green chili, cumin, chaat masala with water — ice cold
Make sweet tamarind water: tamarind paste, sugar, chaat masala, water
Crack a hole in the top of each puri with your thumb
Add a spoonful of potato-chickpea filling
Fill with mint pani — the cold spicy water floods the puri
EAT IMMEDIATELY — in one bite, the whole thing at once
The explosion of cold, spicy, tangy, crunchy in your mouth is the experience
Pani puri is eaten standing at street stalls — the vendor hands them one at a time
You don't stop until you can't eat one more
snacks.description: India's most exhilarating street food — hollow crispy balls filled with spicy mint water, tamarind, and potato, eaten whole in one explosive bite. The cold-spicy-tangy-crunchy sensory overload and the 'one at a time from the vendor' ritual make pani puri the most viral Indian street food and the most fun you can have eating.

snacks.name: Vada Pav (Mumbai's Burger)
ingredients: Vada: potato ball coated in gram flour batter, deep fried
Dry garlic chutney (red, spicy — the secret weapon)
instructions: Make vada: mash potato with green chili, turmeric, mustard seeds, curry leaves
Shape into balls, dip in gram flour batter
Deep fry until golden and crispy
Toast pav with butter on a griddle
Spread green chutney on one side, dry garlic chutney on the other
Place hot vada inside, add fried green chili
Press together — eat with both hands
This is Mumbai's burger — invented in the 1960s-70s as worker food
Costs less than a dollar — feeds a person for hours
Mumbai runs on vada pav — it's not an exaggeration
snacks.description: Mumbai's burger — a spicy potato fritter in a buttered bread roll with three chutneys. Invented as worker food in 1960s Mumbai, vada pav costs less than a dollar and fuels the entire city. The simplicity, the price, and the 'Mumbai's answer to the burger' narrative make vada pav perpetually viral.

snacks.name: Chaat (Street Snack Platter)
ingredients: Chaat masala, cumin powder, red chili
instructions: Arrange papdi or crushed samosa on a plate
Top with potato and chickpeas
Drizzle yogurt over everything — generous
Add tamarind chutney (sweet, dark) and green chutney (spicy)
Sprinkle chaat masala, cumin, red chili
Top with sev (crispy noodles) and pomegranate seeds
The key is eating it immediately — before the crispy elements get soggy
Every bite should have all elements: crispy, creamy, sweet, sour, spicy
Chaat represents Indian flavor philosophy: all tastes in every bite
Delhi's chaat culture is legendary — entire streets dedicated to chaat vendors
snacks.description: India's street snack philosophy — crispy, creamy, sweet, sour, spicy all in every bite. Chaat is less a recipe and more a flavor principle: layer textures and tastes until every bite is a sensory explosion. Delhi's chaat streets and the eat-it-before-it-gets-soggy urgency are perpetually viral.

desserts.name: Gulab Jamun
ingredients: Khoya (reduced milk solids) or milk powder
Sugar syrup: sugar, water, cardamom, rose water, saffron
instructions: Make sugar syrup: boil sugar and water, add cardamom, rose water, saffron — keep warm
Mix khoya (or milk powder) with flour, baking soda, cardamom
Knead gently into a soft dough — do NOT overwork or they'll be hard
Shape into smooth balls — any cracks will cause them to break while frying
Fry in ghee on LOW heat — very low, very slow, very patient
They must be deep brown, evenly colored — rush it and they're raw inside
Immediately drop hot fried balls into warm sugar syrup
Let soak minimum 2 hours — overnight is better
They should be spongy, soaked through, and weep syrup when bitten
Gulab jamun is India's most popular dessert — at every wedding, every celebration
desserts.description: India's most beloved sweet — fried milk-dough balls soaked in rose-cardamom-saffron syrup until they become spongy, syrup-weeping orbs. Served at every wedding, every celebration, every festival. The syrup-weeping cross-section and the 'how are these so soft?' texture make gulab jamun the most viral Indian dessert.

desserts.name: Jalebi
ingredients: Batter: flour (maida), yogurt, saffron, water — fermented
Sugar syrup: sugar, water, cardamom, saffron, lime juice
instructions: Make batter: flour, yogurt, water — ferment 12-24 hours for the sour tang
The fermentation is optional but traditional — it adds complexity
Make sugar syrup with saffron, cardamom, lime juice — keep warm
Pour batter into a squeeze bottle or cloth with a hole
Squeeze batter into hot oil in spiral/pretzel shapes — the shape is the art
Fry until golden and crispy — 2-3 min
Immediately dip in sugar syrup — the hot jalebi absorbs the cold syrup
The temperature contrast is important: hot jalebi, room-temp syrup
The outside should be crispy, the inside should be syrup-filled and hollow
Every bite should crunch then flood with saffron syrup
desserts.description: India's crispy-syrupy spiral — fermented batter piped into hot oil in spirals, fried crispy, then soaked in saffron syrup. The crunch-then-syrup-flood sensation and the mesmerizing spiral-piping technique make jalebi one of the most viral Indian sweets and an ASMR favorite.

desserts.name: Rasmalai
ingredients: Chenna (fresh paneer — made from curdled milk)
instructions: Make chenna: boil milk, add lemon juice to curdle, strain, squeeze dry
Knead chenna until completely smooth — no graininess, this takes effort
Shape into flat discs
Poach discs in sugar syrup — they expand, so make them smaller than final size
Make the ras (sauce): reduce full-fat milk by half — stirring constantly to prevent scorching
Add cardamom, saffron, sugar, rose water to the reduced milk
Place the poached chenna discs in the saffron-pistachio milk
Chill — serve cold, garnished with pistachios and saffron strands
The chenna should be spongy, the milk sauce should be thick and golden
Rasmalai is Bengali in origin — Bengal's dessert tradition is India's finest
desserts.description: Bengali India's most elegant sweet — soft fresh-cheese discs floating in reduced saffron-pistachio-cardamom milk. Rasmalai is Indian dessert at its most refined: the silky chenna, the golden milk, the pistachio garnish. The 'cheese floating in flavored milk' concept surprises and enchants first-timers.

desserts.name: Kheer (Rice Pudding)
instructions: Wash rice, soak 30 min
Boil milk in a heavy-bottomed pot — stir frequently to prevent scorching
Add rice, cook on low heat, stirring often
The rice slowly breaks down and the milk reduces — 35-45 min
The mixture thickens as the starch releases and milk concentrates
Add sugar, cardamom, saffron, nuts, raisins
Add rose water at the end — off heat
The consistency should be thick, creamy, with visible rice grains
Serve warm or cold — both are traditional
Kheer is India's oldest dessert — mentioned in ancient texts
desserts.description: India's ancient rice pudding — rice slowly cooked in reducing milk until thick and creamy, perfumed with cardamom, saffron, and rose water. Mentioned in texts thousands of years old, kheer is India's oldest sweet and the template for rice puddings worldwide.

drinks.name: Masala Chai
ingredients: Spices: ginger (fresh, crushed), cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, black pepper
instructions: Crush ginger and cardamom — release the oils
Boil water with ginger and spices — let the spices infuse 3-5 min
Add tea leaves — boil together (yes, boil — this is not steeping)
Add milk — bring to a rolling boil again
The chai should rise in the pot — watch for the dramatic rise
Strain into cups, add sugar
The color should be a rich caramel-brown
The ginger and cardamom should be prominent — not subtle
Masala chai is India's universal drink — 3+ billion cups consumed daily
The chai wallah (tea vendor) is India's most ubiquitous entrepreneur
drinks.description: India's spiced milk tea — black tea boiled (not steeped) with ginger, cardamom, and milk. Over 3 billion cups consumed daily across India. The dramatic pot-rise, the chai wallah street vendors, and the 'this is not a chai latte' distinction from Western versions make masala chai perpetually viral.

drinks.name: Mango Lassi
ingredients: Ripe mango (Alphonso for the best flavor)
instructions: Blend ripe mango with yogurt — the ratio should favor the mango
Add sugar, cardamom, ice
Blend until thick and frothy
The color should be a beautiful sunset orange-gold
Garnish with saffron strands if desired
Serve cold — this is India's answer to the milkshake
Alphonso mangoes (available April-June) make the best lassi
The yogurt adds tang that balances the mango sweetness
Mango lassi is the gateway Indian drink — everyone loves it
drinks.description: India's mango-yogurt smoothie — ripe mango blended with yogurt and cardamom into a thick, sunset-colored drink. The gateway to Indian drinks for the entire world. Alphonso mango season (April-June) produces the finest lassi, and the yogurt-tang-against-mango-sweet balance is perfection.

drinks.name: Thandai (Festival Milk Drink)
instructions: Soak all nuts and seeds in water for 2+ hours
Grind into a smooth paste with saffron, cardamom, rose petals
Mix the paste into cold milk — the milk turns a pale gold-pink
Add sugar, stir until dissolved
Strain if desired — traditional thandai is smooth
Serve very cold — this is a festive drink for Holi and Shivratri
The nut-milk combination is incredibly rich and fragrant
The saffron-rose-cardamom flavor profile is quintessentially Indian
Some versions include bhang (cannabis) for Holi — the legal, traditional version
Without bhang, it's a magnificent spiced nut milk
drinks.description: India's festival milk drink — almonds, pistachios, saffron, and rose petals ground into cold milk for a pale gold, fragrant, rich drink. Served at Holi and Shivratri. The nut-milk richness and the festival connection (some versions traditionally include bhang/cannabis for Holi) make thandai annually viral.

drinks.name: Filter Coffee (South Indian)
ingredients: Filter coffee powder (Arabica-Robusta blend, chicory added — South Indian style)
South Indian coffee filter (brass or stainless steel)
instructions: Add coffee powder to the upper chamber of the South Indian filter
Pour boiling water on top, close the lid — let it drip through slowly
The decoction drips for 10-15 min — strong, concentrated coffee
Boil milk separately — it must be hot and frothy
In a tumbler (dabarah), mix decoction with hot milk and sugar
Pour from one vessel to another at arm's height — the 'pulling' technique
The pulling aerates the coffee and creates a frothy top
The height of the pour shows skill — the longer the stream, the better
South Indian filter coffee is a ritual — the brass filter, the pulling, the tumbler
This is the coffee tradition that predates espresso culture in India
drinks.description: South India's filter coffee — strong decoction from a brass filter mixed with hot milk and 'pulled' from height to create froth. The dramatic arm's-length pour, the brass filter, and the tumbler-and-dabarah vessels make South Indian filter coffee one of the most theatrical and viral coffee preparations in the world.
